architecture.decision: Independent token namespaces. --yuri-hud-* and --yuri-kagami-*. No base+override. Cross-surface reuse = hard error.

entries.decision: Design Master now requires a 10-question intake/mapping gate and promotes Marcel visual corrections into structured design memory before future design output.
entries.rationale: The prior presentation drifted into boxed logbook/deck grammar because preferences were treated as session context instead of durable system input.
entries.pattern: design brief -> skill selection -> output -> verification -> memory promotion

entries.decision: Split YURI into independent HUD and Kagami namespaces, then bind motion and token selection to the active surface.
entries.rationale: HUD remains the operator shell while Kagami remains the editorial/cinematic shell; shared tokens caused false overrides.

entries.decision: Preserve the Kagami sprint-audit template as the reusable fork baseline for cover, atmos, portal, and alternating S0 beats.
entries.rationale: The template captures the stable Kagami fork shape and should remain available without overruling HUD canonical tokens.

designIntake.rule: Ask at least 10 design questions before producing new design output, or map an already-approved user brief to these categories and ask only for missing answers.

kagamiPresentation.output_shape: continuous HTML presentation, not slide deck
kagamiPresentation.density: dense but composed; avoid sparse one-point slides
kagamiPresentation.structure: typography, motion, mirror geometry, lines, seals, and spatial rhythm over boxed/card-heavy layout
kagamiPresentation.motion: visible scroll choreography, camera movement, parallax, masks, text motion, and reduced-motion fallback
dislikes: HUD language or operator dashboard grammar on Kagami surfaces
sharp square blocks as the main grammar
kagamiPresentation.success_test: Feels like a polished cinematic Kagami briefing with varied composition and visible motion design.
kagamiPresentation.memory_policy: promote as reusable Kagami presentation preference

skillOrchestration.selectionRule: Pick skills from the local YURI tree based on the Design Brief; do not default to a single generic frontend skill.
